title: The Fox News Effect: Media Bias and Voting

original_reference.notes: The paper reports 0.0042 (0.0015). Weighted OLS with all 42 original controls and 235 district intercepts; cable-system clustered CR1 covariance counts the full design rank, matching the original areg specification.

id_source_row.description: One-based row number in the unchanged author-prepared data file.

id_district.description: Original congressional-district identifier; use the supplied fixed indicators as controls.

y.description: Republican two-party presidential vote share in 2000 minus its 1996 share. Multiply a coefficient by 100 to express it in percentage points.

d.description: Fox News was available on the town's local cable system in 2000.

weight.description: Total presidential votes in 1996, used as the original regression weight.

cluster_id.description: One-based factor code for the original cable-system identifier; towns sharing a cable system share a code.

sample_notes: The unchanged prepared author file has 10,126 rows; sample12000 == 1 yields the original 9,256-town regression sample.
All required original variables are finite and complete in that sample, and all regression weights are positive; no additional rows are lost.
The outcome is already a 2000-minus-1996 change. Each town occupies one row; no panel reshaping or panel estimator is needed.
The 42 original substantive controls are 24 census terms and 18 cable-system decile indicators. No original control is replaced, logged, or supplemented with another baseline covariate.
The 234 supplied district indicators omit district code 1; include an intercept. Cable-system clusters total 2,992.
The original census levels, original differences and precomputed outcome retain their exact stored values; converting them to float64 does not recreate the authors' earlier calculations.
identification_notes: The exposure is local cable availability, not individual Fox viewing. The estimate is a conditional difference in Republican vote-share growth.
Nonrandom Fox rollout and unobserved differences in electoral trends remain identification concerns.
The original census controls include contemporaneous 2000 values. They must not be described as an entirely pre-treatment adjustment set.
The original regression includes district indicators and standard errors clustered by cable system.

provenance.transformations: Filter the original sample flag, retain the exact original numeric variables, rename columns, encode cable-system IDs, and supply district indicators with the first sorted level omitted.
